_comment: Declarative SSOT for the internal Bugzilla (5.2) project/lifecycle configuration.
setup-projects.pl converges the installation to this state; verify-projects.py asserts it.
REBASED ON REALITY (spec_version 2.0.0). The installation is NOT empty: four products
already exist and OptionsEdge holds 177 live bugs created 2026-06-11..2026-08-03. Two hard
constraints follow from that, and they shape everything below:
1. the four existing products are adopted, not replaced;
2. no existing bug's DATA may be modified.
Constraint 2 stated precisely, because the difference matters. Adding a custom field is NOT
free: Bugzilla defines a single-select as varchar(64) NOT NULL DEFAULT '---' (Field.pm
SQL_DEFINITIONS), so the ALTER TABLE writes that unset sentinel into all 177 existing rows,
and the ALTER may rebuild the table physically depending on the MariaDB version. There is no
NULL-able custom field in Bugzilla, so no category field can be added without this.
What IS guaranteed, and proven on every run: that is ALL that happens to them. No status,
resolution, product or any other existing field of any existing bug changes - the provisioner
digests every pre-existing column before and after and requires them byte-for-byte identical,
and separately asserts each new column holds exactly '---' on every pre-existing row.
Constraint 2 is why there is no cf_issue_type (a mandatory select over a populated table
gives every existing row the '---' sentinel) and why CONFIRMED/IN_PROGRESS are NOT renamed
(Bugzilla/Field/Choice.pm:158 implements a value rename as UPDATE bugs SET <field> = ?,
which would rewrite 80 live rows). The issue type is derived from the product instead, and
cf_category is optional.
_enforcement_switch_comment: There is deliberately NO 'enforcement enabled' parameter: anyone with tweakparams could
turn one off. The extension derives its state instead, anchored on cf_category - the one
object this design creates. Absent outside a web/API request = never provisioned
(bootstrap, nothing enforced, so checksetup.pl and the provisioner can run). Absent or
structurally damaged during a request = BROKEN: every guarded change is refused until
_product_type_comment: The issue type IS the product. bugs.product_id is already the normalised ownership column;
storing the type a second time per bug would create two authorities that can drift, and
could not be populated for the 177 existing rows anyway. Product changes are recorded in
bug activity, so history stays reconstructible.
Search ergonomics: 'all bugs' is product IN (OptionsEdge, Fullfunding).
_product_type_id_comment: Product NAMES are mutable, so a name-only map can be subverted: rename OptionsEdge aside,
rename a requirement product into its place, rename back, and 177 bugs are derived as
REQUIREMENTs without a single bug row changing. The id cannot be edited from the admin UI,
so name and id must BOTH agree or the installation goes fail-closed.
These ids are installation-specific by nature; this repository configures one installation.

_comment: OPTIONAL, and deliberately uncontrolled. Bugzilla stores one visibility_value_id per
choice row, so a product-controlled vocabulary would need per-product duplicates of
every value (there are two products per type) - which would fragment reporting and
strand values on a same-type product move. One flat BUG_*/REQ_* list, with the
extension rejecting a value that does not belong to the item's product-derived type.
Optional is what leaves the 177 existing bugs alone: an empty category is always valid.
Controlled by product rather than by a type field: the two BUG products are exactly the
places an environment makes sense, and product IS a select field Bugzilla accepts as a
controller (FIELD_TYPE_SINGLE_SELECT, Field/Choice.pm CLASS_MAP maps it to
Bugzilla::Product).

_statuses_comment: The BUG branch keeps Bugzilla's stock names. Renaming CONFIRMED/IN_PROGRESS would be an
UPDATE against the 80 live bugs sitting on them (Field/Choice.pm:158), which the no-touch
constraint forbids. Only the four REQ_* statuses are new, so no bug's status value is
The REQ_ prefix still makes a cross-branch status obvious to a human; the extension is what
makes it impossible. Existing sortkeys are kept exactly as they are (100/200/300/400/500) so
no existing row is rewritten; the new REQ_* statuses take 600-900.
'exists' records which statuses are expected to be there already - the provisioner refuses
to CREATE one marked true, because that would mean the installation is not what we think.
_workflow_comment: Installation-wide matrix (bug_status + status_workflow are global in Bugzilla - there is no
per-product or per-type workflow). Both lifecycles live in this one matrix; the
IssueTypeWorkflow extension is what stops an item crossing between the two branches.
'' (empty from) is the bug-creation row (status_workflow.old_status IS NULL).
Every status must be able to reach duplicate_or_move_bug_status (RESOLVED), otherwise
Bugzilla::Status::add_missing_bug_status_transitions() re-adds the row behind our back.
Rewriting status_workflow does NOT touch bug rows.
_enforcement_comment: Mirrored as Perl constants in extensions/IssueTypeWorkflow/Extension.pm, which the
provisioner refuses to run against if the two disagree. The constants exist so that an
unreadable or half-written config file can never silently turn enforcement off.

_error_codes_comment: illegal_change (115) is core Bugzilla's, raised whenever the extension denies an UPDATE
via priv_results; REST maps it to HTTP 401. The 1000xx codes are the extension's own,
registered through the webservice_error_codes hook and mapped to HTTP 400.
verify-projects.py asserts these exact codes so an auth failure, a 404 or a 500 can never
The two initial_status codes are race defence: a damaged workflow normally trips
issue_type_workflow_misconfigured first. The verifier says which it cannot induce.

_component_owner_comment: default_assignee is declared here rather than passed on the command line, so two runs with
different arguments cannot produce two different installations from the same SSOT.
--default-assignee remains as the fallback for a component that does not name one.
_products_comment: These four already exist - created by separate work, with OptionsEdge holding the 177 live
bugs. They are adopted as they are; only descriptions are converged (the OptionsEdge
General component still carries Bugzilla's TestProduct boilerplate, because that product
began life as TestProduct and was renamed).
Component/version/milestone sets are declared exactly as they exist so the provisioner
neither adds nor removes anything the other work owns.
